headline: Approved a ban on e-motos on city recreation paths, updates to ordinances on unmet social needs, and a Howard Center caseworker contract.
summary: The city adopted ordinance updates covering drug paraphernalia disposal, medians, and littering. It also banned e-motos on city recreation paths and approved a contract with the Howard Center for a 30-hour-per-week caseworker in the Police Department. It approved the FY 28 budget schedule and began a process to develop a 2027 legislative agenda.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including disbursements, 2026 road and bridge standards, a DPW construction contract, and truck financing, by a 3-0 vote.
Adopted updates to city ordinance chapters 14, 20, 43, and 36 and rescinded Council Policy 2022-05 and 2025-03, by a 3-0 vote.
Approved updates to ordinance Chapters 22 and 36, which prohibit e-motos on city recreation paths, by a 3-0 vote.
Approved the contract with the Howard Center for a caseworker to connect people with unmet social needs to services, by a 3-0 vote.
Approved the FY 28 Budget Schedule, by a 3-0 vote.
Approved the process to develop a 2027 Legislative agenda, by a 3-0 vote.
Designated Jessie Baker as voting delegate to the Vermont League of Cities and Towns annual meeting, by a 3-0 vote.
Approved the liquor and tobacco license applications for Stewart's Shop #507, Stewart's Shop 504, Top Choice Convenience & Tobacco, LLC, and Zachary's Pizza, by a 3-0 vote.
Postponed the executive session on Development Review Board appointments until the second candidate's interest is confirmed.

CITY COUNCIL
8 SEPTEMBER 2026
The South Burlington City Council held a regular meeting on Tuesday, 8
September 2026, at 6: 30 p. m., in the Auditorium, 180 Market Street, and by
Zoom.
MEMBERS PRESENT: T. Barritt, Chair; E. Fitzgerald, A. Chalnick,
ALSO PRESENT: J. Baker, City Manager; N. Storellicastro, Deputy City Manager;
C. McNeil, City Attorney; Chief W. Breault, Police Department; Chief C. Corbin, Fire
Department; M. Machar, Finance Director; A. Pugh, T. Grayson, C. Hartman, L.
Marriott, M. Sypes
1.  Pledge of Allegiance:
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited.
2. Instructions on exiting the building in case of emergency and review of
technology options:
Ms. Baker provided instructions on emergency exit from the building and
reviewed technology options.
3.  Additions, deletions or changes in the order of Agenda items:
No changes were made to the Agenda.
4.  Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda:
Mr. Sypes asked if the Council can help with an issue involving mail delivery.
Residents of Dorset Farms have been getting only a little of their mail.  They have
PAGE 1
been told by USPS that they are a " rural route" and that they have to go to Pine
Street to get their mail.  They would appreciate any help the City can give them.
Mr. Hartman said he has created a " First Step Vermont" app of resources for
people in need.  He said this is a first step to get them help.  Ms. Baker thanked
Mr. Hartman for connecting with Chief Breault.
Ms. Marriott noted issues at Red Rocks Park need attention including serious
erosion and damage to the rock wall which supports the trails.  She said she has
some suggestions as to what to do. Ms. Marriott noted that Mr. Storellicastro had
called her today. Mr. Chalnick suggested Ms. Marriott contact Mr. Storellicastro
and/ or Public Works people who can bring the issues to the Council.
5.  Councilors Announcements and Reports on Committee Assignments
and City Manager' s Report:
Council members reported on recent meetings and events they had attended.
Ms. Baker: The 21 September Council meeting has been rescheduled for 22
September.
The " Green Festival" on 19 September is in need of volunteers.
Volunteers are also needed for the Fly By 5K event at the Airport.
The Secretary of State' s office will be mailing ballots for the 3
November election on 21 September.  City Hall will then become a voting center
with no campaigning allowed.
There is an application at the DRB for subdivision and conversion of a
congregate care building to apartments.
The Tier 1A application is in, and there will be a site visit this week.  The
City will hear the response later in the fall.
Work on Garden Street continues, and the road will open in late
November.
The Economic Mobility Program, of which the City is a member, had its
first presentation in August.  The program serves people who are looking to grow
their businesses.
CITY COUNCIL 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 2
Ms. Baker thanked the Recreation Department for hosting a number of
concurrent events during a 24-hour period last week.
6.  Consent Agenda:
a.  Consider and Sign Disbursements
b.  Adopt 2026 Town Road and Bridge Standards
c.  Award the construction contract for the DPW Site Improvements
project to SD Ireland and authorize the Interim Director of Public
Works to execute and manage the contract
d.  Approve the truck financing
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to approve the Consent Agenda as presented.  Mr. Barritt
seconded.  Motion passed 3- 0.
NOTE: Some of the following Agenda items were heard out of order but will be
recorded here in the order they appeared on the agenda.
7.  Warned for 7 p. m., Hold a second reading and Public Hearing on
updates to South Burlington City Ordinance Chapter 14
Environment), Chapter 20 ( Miscellaneous Offenses), Chapter 32
Streets, Sidewalks and Other Public Spaces), and Chapter 36 ( Traffic
and Vehicles) and rescind City Council Policy 2022- 05 and 2025-03.
These changes address behaviors related to unmet social needs that
impact both an individual' s quality of life and the quality of life of the
greater community:
Chief Breault said these updates will provide Officers with a tool to help get
people with unmet social needs to appropriate services.
Mr. McNeil noted that the Ordinance prohibiting people from standing on
medians is a safety measure.
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to read the Ordinance by Title and to open a public hearing
on updates to Chapter 14 ( Environment), Chapter 20 ( Miscellaneous Offenses),
Chapter 32 ( Streets, Sidewalks and other Public Spaces) and Chapter 36 ( Traffic
and Vehicles).  Mr. Barritt seconded.  Motion passed 3- 0.
Chief Breault noted that Chapter 14 includes safe disposal of drug paraphernalia.
This is to prevent contact by children.  In addition, alcohol cannot be consumed in
CITY COUNCIL 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 3
public, nor can there be open containers of alcohol in public spaces without a
permit.
Mr. McNeil said there is also a provision against littering in the City.
Mr. Chalnick asked for public comment.  There was no public comment.
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to close the public hearing.  Mr. Barritt seconded.  Motion
passed 3-0.
8.  Possibly approve updates to South Burlington City Ordinance
Chapter 14 ( Environment), Chapter 20 ( Miscellaneous Offenses),
Chapter 32 ( Streets, Sidewalks and Other Public Spaces), and
Chapter 36 (Traffic and Vehicles) and rescind Council Policy 2022-05
and 2025- 03:
Ms. Fitzgerald said she was contacted by a person who does clean- up, which can
include drug paraphernalia.  That person asked if any appropriate container is
allowed. Chief Breault said it is as long as the paraphernalia is not exposed.
Ms. Fitzgerald said the same person asked about " soliciting" on medians.  Chief
Breault said asking from money is a constitutional protected act but must be done
so in a safe location.  He cited a recent accident in which a vehicle wound up on a
median in a place where a solicitor often sits and would have been seriously
injured.  Mr. McNeil added that most medians are very narrow.
Ms. Fitzgerald asked if bus stops are non- smoking areas.  Staff will check on this
as no one present was sure.
Ms. Fitzgerald then moved to adopt the updates to South Burlington Ordinances
Chapters 14, 20, 43, and 36 as presented and rescind Council Policy 2022-05 and
2025- 03. Mr. Barritt seconded.  Motion passed 3-0.
9.  Warned for 7: 00 p. m.: Hold a Second Reading and Public Hearing on
updates to South Burlington City Ordinance Chapter 22 ( Parks and
Recreation) and Chapter 36 ( Traffic and Vehicles).  These changes
address electric mobility devices as recommended by the Bicycle and
Pedestrian Committee:
CITY COUNCIL 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 4
Chief Breault said these updates are in response to complaints the Police
Department has received and to requests from the Bike/ Ped Committee.  What
was previously in Chapter 22 has been moved to Chapter 36.  The updates
prohibit e-motos on the City' s rec paths.
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to read the Ordinances by Title and to open a public hearing
on updates to Chapter 22 ( Parks and Recreation) and Chapter 36 ( Traffic and
Vehicles).  Mr. Barritt seconded.  Motion passed 3- 0.
Mr. Chalnick asked for public comment.  There was no public comment.
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to close the public hearing.  Mr. Barritt seconded.  Motion
passed 3-0.
10.Possibly approve updates to South Burlington City Ordinance
Chapter 22 ( Parks and Recreation) and Chapter 36 ( Traffic and
Vehicles):
Ms. Fitzgerald felt this was a move in the right direction, but what is being
marketed to youth may require an ongoing conversation and is something to keep
an eye on.
Mr. Chalnick noted that State Law already covers most of this.  The city is
prohibiting e- motos on rec paths even if the driver is licensed and the vehicle is
registered.
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to approve updates to South Burlington City Ordinances
Chapters 22 and 36 as presented.  Mr. Barritt seconded.  Motion passed 3- 0.
11. Approve Contract with Howard Center to support a Service
Coordinator to connect individuals with unmet social needs to
appropriate social services as part of the City' s overall response to
assisting individuals experiencing an unmet social need.
Chief Breault said there is now an agreement with the Howard Center that will
help to meet the needs of people in the community with unmet social needs.  The
agreement is for a 30- hour- per- week Caseworker embedded in the Police
Department.   The aim is to eliminate future police involvement.  The program will
continue to be developed over the coming years based on data.
CITY COUNCIL 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 5
Mr. Hartman said this program will fit well with the First Step Vermont program
with the hope of helping everyone involved.
Ms. Fitzgerald noted that Chief Breault had already responded to a number of her
questions regarding credentials, monitoring, etc.  She also noted there could be
up to a $ 77, 000 expenditure for such things as mileage and supervision.  Chief
Breault said that is a worst- case scenario, and he didn' t anticipate anything like
that amount.  He also noted that opiate funding that the city has received would
cover such costs.  Members agreed this was a very good use of those funds and
expressed the hope that the program would be very successful.
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to approve the contract with the Howard Center as
presented.  Mr. Barritt seconded.  Motion passed 3- 0.
12. Interview Development Review Board Candidates:
The Council interviewed Theodore Reicin for appointment to the Development
Review Board.
The other potential candidate was not present, and members agreed to interview
him if he later arrived.
13.Receive a presentation from the Champlain Valley Office of
Economic Opportunity on plans to locate a 100- bed low- barrier
shelter at 1717 Williston Road:
Ms. Baker noted that CVOEO had requested to remove their attendance from this
Agenda.  She added that the Council has no action to take at this meeting.
Ms. Baker said the City is encouraging CVOEO and Champlain Housing Trust to
engage in deep community engagement.  She noted that in May, staff met with
those organizations to discuss the concept of having a low barrier shelter
somewhere in Chittenden County.  On August 24th CVOEO and CHT presented
plans for such a shelter at 1717 Williston Road.
Ms. Baker stressed that the city is open to working in partnership with CVOEO and
CHT on a service and location that best meet the needs of our neighbors.
Mr. Chalnick expressed the hope that the City can work with those groups
regarding a facility in the right place and of the right size.
CITY COUNCIL 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 6
Ms. Fitzgerald said she felt the City asked the right questions and also felt the
community would have questions.  She shared the concern with location and size
and supported ongoing conversations including staffing and budget implications.
Mr. Barritt enumerated the numerous affordable housing locations that the City
has supported in past years.  He, too, wanted the conversation to continue.
Public comment was solicited.  There was no public comment.
14.Discuss and possibly approve the FY 28 Budget Schedule:
Ms. Machar drew attention to the schedule outline and process.  She noted that
the Budget Retreat is scheduled for 16 December.  This will be preceded by goal
setting on 22 September and by public listening sessions.
Ms. Machar noted that new software is very accurate and eliminates the
possibility of errors.  It is also very time saving.
Mr. Chalnick moved to approve the FY 28 Budget Schedule as presented.  Ms.
Fitzgerald seconded.  Motion passed 3- 0.
15.Discuss and possibly approve a process to develop a 2027 Legislative
agenda:
Mr. Storellicastro cited the importance of having a voice in the Legislative process
and said the more specific that voice is, the better.
Ms. Baker suggested an early meeting with the City' s current delegation and 2
City Councilors.  She noted that Dr. Zigmund has expressed an interest in being
one of those delegates.  Other Council members also expressed their interest.
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to approve the process to develop a Legislative agenda.  Mr.
Chalnick seconded.  Motion passed 3-0.
Ms. Pugh noted that with a November 3rdelection, it is important not to give the
impression that the City is supporting certain candidates and recognize availability
may be limited due to campaigning.
CITY COUNCIL 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 7
16.Designate a Voting Delegate to the Vermont League of Cities and
Towns annual meeting scheduled for Town Fair on 6 October 2026:
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to designate Jessie Baker as Voting Delegate to the
Vermont League of Cities and Towns annual meeting.  Mr. Barritt seconded.  The
motion passed 3-0.
17.Convene as Liquor Control Commission to consider the following
applications for approval: Stewart' s Shop # 507, Second Class Liquor
License, Tobacco/ Tobacco Substitute Endorsement; Stewart' s Shop
504, Second Class Liquor License, Tobacco/ Tobacco Substitute
Endorsement; Top Choice Convenience & Tobacco, LLC,
Tobacco/ Tobacco Substitute Endorsement; Zachary' s Pizza, Third
Class Liquor License:
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to convene as Liquor Control Commission.  Mr. Barritt
seconded.  Motion passed 3-0.
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to approve the applications for approval as presented.  Mr.
Barritt seconded.  Motion passed 3-0.
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to reconvene as City Council.  Mr. Barritt seconded.  Motion
passed 3- 0.
18. Review the significant agenda topics below for the Council' s 21
September 2026 Council Meeting:
a.  East Terrace Residents re: traffic calming
b.  Receive the FY26 year end projections
c.  FY28 Budget: Receive projections from staff and establish goals
for the FY28 Budget
d.  Receive the FY27 Policy, Priorities and Strategies — Report # 1
Ms. Baker suggested removing item " d."
19. Other Business:
Ms. Fitzgerald suggested an agenda item to discuss improvement to the process
of capital improvement funding and the monitoring of high visibility projects and
those which have exceeded original budgeted amounts or engineering estimates
CITY COUNCIL 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 8
to includesuch projectsasthe BartlettBayWasteWaterTreatmentFacility, the
TIF District and the 1-89 bike/ped bridge. After action discussions may assist
process improvements.
Ms. Fitzgerald suggested discussing a standard for responding to communication
from residents who raise questions/ issues.  She noted that at this time, some
people get a response while others do not. Media response may be another area
to discuss.
20. Considering entering an executive session, pursuant to 1 V.S.A.
Section 313(a)(3) for the purpose of discussing appointments to the
Development Review Board:
As the second DRBcandidate did not appear, members agreed to postpone the
Executive Session to determine if he is still interested.
As there was no further business to come before the Council, Mr. Chalnick moved
to adjourn.  Ms. Fitzgerald seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.  The meeting
was adjourned at 8: 12 p. m.
